items.title: EMCOR Q3 Earnings Beat on Construction Strength, '26 Outlook Raised
items.summary: EMCOR Group reported Q3 2026 earnings of $9.60 per share, up 46.1% YoY and beating estimates by 15.3%, with revenues rising 28.8% to $5.54 billion. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenues ($20.6-$21B) and EPS ($34.50-$35.50), driven by strong demand in electrical and mechanical construction. Record remaining performance obligations of $18.57 billion indicate sustained demand for mission-critical infrastructure.

items.title: EMCOR Stock Trades at a Premium: Should Investors Buy or Steer Clear?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported strong first-half 2026 results with 19.7% revenue growth to $9.78 billion, driven by robust demand for data centers, AI infrastructure, and healthcare projects. The company raised full-year guidance and achieved record backlog of $17.14 billion. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (21.46x forward P/E) compared to peers, and faces headwinds from inflation, labor shortages, and supply-chain disruptions.

items.title: EMCOR Rises 21% Year to Date: Should Investors Buy the Stock Now?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) has gained 21.2% year-to-date, outperforming its industry peers. The company benefits from strong demand across data centers, industrial, and construction markets, with Electrical Construction revenues up 24% and Mechanical Construction up 31% in Q2 2026. Record RPOs of $17.14 billion (up 44% YoY) and raised 2026 guidance to $20-$20.5 billion in revenue provide strong growth visibility. However, EME trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/E of 20.7 compared to industry peers.
